text:
Broad relevance does not establish a compelling next choice. [Aspect-level complementarity research](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0950705122010292) distinguishes general co-occurrence from complements suited to particular user intents; [CoDeR](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/33379) studies demand shifts obscured by noisy histories. These motivate diagnostic hypotheses: within similarly relevant candidate pairs, does the model favor documented compatibility over vague similarity, added capability over duplication, and recent-interest evidence over older topical overlap? Title/description evidence can support these comparisons, but cannot establish ownership, mood, or actual need.

Negative feedback needs separate interpretation. [Interpreting User Inaction](https://will-qianzhao.github.io/pubs/zhao2018recsys-a.pdf) distinguishes reasons including “not now,” “explore later,” and “would not enjoy”; nonselection therefore cannot automatically mean rejection. Proposed feedback coding: explicit rejection, deferred interest, positive interest, and unresolved identification, retaining evidence excerpts. Missing or ambiguous metadata should yield an unknown judgment rather than incompatibility. These are proposed diagnostic rules, not validated preference labels; no supplied qualitative feedback was available here to measure their agreement.

For paired tests, record the trained model’s score difference, evidence-backed expected ordering, ties, and abstentions; report agreement alongside metadata coverage and feedback counts per category. Swap candidate presentation order and conceal model identity when using language-model judges: [recommendation-specific research](https://research.atspotify.com/publications/intent-description-anchoring-bias-in-llm-as-a-judge-evaluation-of-recommendation-systems) found that algorithm descriptions changed judgments of identical recommendations. Validate proxies against explicit qualitative statements, inspect disagreements, and keep these diagnostics separate from the fixed macro validation HR@10 selection metric.
